install_tell: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/longhorn/longhorn/master/deploy/longhorn.yaml  (longhorn-frontend Service exposes the UI/API)
misconfig_patterns: longhorn-frontend / longhorn-manager /v1 API served without auth when ingress lacks basic-auth/oauth2-proxy — /v1/backup* returns JSON volume/backup names, sizes, timestamps, and the S3/NFS backup-target URL

AI-scope discriminator: Longhorn is generic K8s block storage; backup endpoints expose only volume/backup NAMES, sizes, timestamps, backup-target URL (no payload). Metadata-only inference: (1) /v1/backupvolumes and /v1/volumes 'name'/'volumeName' is the PVC name — in-scope only when it names an AI/ML workload (qdrant, weaviate, milvus, chroma, pgvector, pinecone-, elasticsearch-vector, mlflow, modelregistry, ollama-models, huggingface-cache, triton, tgi, vllm, kserve, ray, feast, label-studio, minio-models, postgres-vector, redis-vector); (2) /v1/backuptargets 'backupTargetURL' (s3://ml-model-backups@.../ or nfs://.../vectordb-snapshots) is the second tell; (3) the volume's kubernetesStatus.workloadsStatus / pvName maps back to the StatefulSet/Deployment (milvus-standalone, weaviate-0). No AI/ML name match = generic substrate, OUT of scope.

Restraint: names-and-metadata only. /v1/backup* enumerates volume names, snapshot names, sizes, timestamps, and the S3/NFS backup-target URL — that inventory is the finding. Do NOT issue restore/download: POST /v1/backupvolumes/{name}?action=backupVolumeRestore or volume snapshotBackup/restore actions are WRITE primitives (create volumes, trigger restores), forbidden. Never pull block data from the s3:// or nfs:// target (exfil). Never read the credentialSecret value, only its name.

response_markers: Rancher-style API browser header X-Api-Schemas / schemaVersion v1
active_probe.false_positive_check: Require a real JSON body marker ("type":"backupTarget" or "type":"backupVolume"), not the HTML title (http.title:Longhorn matches docs/blog/Helm-chart/Rancher pages with no live API). Other Rancher/go-rancher v1 services (Rancher, Harvester) share the envelope ("resourceType":"collection", links, actions, schemaVersion) — disambiguate by Longhorn-specific resource type values backupTarget/backupVolume/snapshot and backupTargetURL, which Rancher/Harvester never expose. A UI behind ingress basic-auth/oauth2-proxy returns 401/403/redirect on /v1/* = surface-open-access-not-exercised. longhorn-frontend on :80 serving only the SPA shell (no /v1 JSON) is UI-only. Catch-all/honeypot echoing the dork in HTML (Insight #107/#108) — require the structured JSON envelope (resourceType:collection + data[] array of typed objects). port 9500 is longhorn-manager's own API/metrics — do not double-count the same host.

deployment_tells: /v1/backuptargets returns backupTargetURL (s3:// or nfs:// destination) + credentialSecret name
/v1/backupvolumes returns typed objects with backupVolumeName/size/lastBackupName in a resourceType:collection envelope
longhorn-ui SPA on :80 with the Rancher-style v1 API browser (X-Api-Schemas header)
pivot_paths: GET /v1/backuptargets -> read backupTargetURL (s3:// or nfs:// destination) + available status + credentialSecret name (name only) — identifies WHERE backups live and whether the bucket name signals AI/ML data
GET /v1/backupvolumes -> enumerate every backed-up volume by backupVolumeName, size, lastBackupName, created timestamp — names only
GET /v1/backupvolumes/{name} -> per-volume detail: dataStored, lastBackupAt, labels (labels often carry the workload/namespace, e.g. app=milvus)
GET /v1/backups/{backupVolumeName} -> list snapshot/backup point-in-time entries (backupName, snapshotName, createdAt) — the snapshot inventory
GET /v1/backups/{backupVolumeName}/{backupName} -> single backup manifest metadata (size, snapshotName, volumeName) — read the manifest, never the blocks
GET /v1/volumes and /v1/volumes/{name} -> live PVC mapping via kubernetesStatus (pvName, namespace, workloadsStatus) to confirm the AI/ML workload behind the volume
GET /v1/settings -> read backup-target config, default replica count, and version string for CVE scoping (read-only)
Stop at the inventory: counting and naming snapshots IS the finding
vulnerabilities: CVE-2021-36780: unauthorized data access from replicas via instance-manager pods (GHSA-27q8-g55w-83p9) — in-cluster gRPC on TCP 8500 unauthenticated, any workload can read/write replica data and exec binaries in the image; fixed v1.1.3
CVE-2021-36779: host operations allowed in privileged Longhorn-managed pods (GHSA-g358-m2wp-mhhx) — privilege-escalation surface via privileged daemon pods; fixed v1.1.3
